chat.author: Mark Atwood
chat.text: The answer to AI volume is AI review. Models are good at finding real defects in drafts: missing case arms, codepoint collisions, broken security claims. They're bad at telling who wrote a message, and that gets worse with every model release. Pangram's error rates in the deck are the vendor's own figures. Spend the $450 a month on review, not on scoring senders.

chat.author: Robert Sparks
chat.text: short response to the assertion that storing the drafts is free. Storing the increasing number of bits all by itself is small cost. Allowing things like search over the content of all the new bits, producting lists of the things, making the things rapidly available, and the other additional load that the extra bits drive is likely still not outrageous, but it _is_ an increase in cost. But the better question is how hard the existance of the extra pile of bits is on the regular participant.
